title: REGRESSION (from RUNTIME-L01 merge): recovery sweep races live prompts — 1/50 standalone iterations lose the event stream
symptom: oc-cli standalone_provider_race::standalone_boot_spawn_loop_custom_provider_stable fails ~1-in-50 iterations: 'step marker does not carry the custom model id' + 'Event stream disconnected during prompt execution'. Bisected: green on pre-C3 main (3448/3448 workspace incl. this test), RED at d313d03 (post runtime-a, pre runtime-b), RED at main
expected: recovery sweep never interferes with sessions claimed by the CURRENT boot: only pre-boot claims are swept (claim time < process start, or equivalent generation guard), mirroring v2 installRestartContinuity semantics (process.ts:104-110: fork after layer build, before ready)
actual: boot.rs recovery_sweep forked before serve; release_child_claims (empty-recoverable arm) resets ALL time_suspended child rows and the resume/replay machinery can terminal-fail or interrupt a session claimed milliseconds earlier by the live server
impact: server restart continuity (L01) can kill in-flight prompts after boot; race window is small but real; blocks batch-1B exit (workspace red)
repro: tools/dev-gate.sh 'CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/opencode/target-main cargo nextest run -p oc-cli -E "test(standalone_boot_spawn_loop_custom_provider_stable)"' (deterministic within ~2 runs; ~1 failure per 50 iterations)

commands: verifier: red reproduced run2 (1-after-49, doubled-turn signature) + green x2 clean; fix audit (strict < bound both arms, boot-entry capture); v2 grounding verbatim; 1123/1123; guards 8/8
evidence.counts: race x2 clean; runtime_recovery 6/6; boot_ 22/22; oc-core+oc-server 1123/1123

notes: FIXED 2026-10-19 by lane-sweepfix @ 9ce1ba1. Root cause (runtime-proven): boot_and_serve forked recovery_sweep unconditionally and its claim queries (list_suspended / release_child_claims) carry no owner signature — time_suspended is the only marker — so a session claimed milliseconds earlier by the CURRENT boot or a concurrently-live peer sharing the DB (the test runs 10 standalone pairs concurrently on one sandbox/DB) was resumed like a dead predecessor's orphan: the peer's execution.resume() started a SECOND concurrent drain of the live session. Evidence: every red iteration prints the FakeLlm greeting TWICE (double-driven turn) before 'Event stream disconnected during prompt execution' kills the run client (red.log / red-run2.log; 2 red runs pre-fix, ~1-2 failures per 50 iterations). Fix: boot_started_ms captured at boot_and_serve entry; sweep uses list_suspended_before / release_child_claims_before — claims recorded strictly before process start only (pre-boot state). v2 grounding: restart.ts:44-52 — the sweep assumes every orphaned claim's owner is dead, an invariant v2 enforces by installing it ONLY under the managed lifecycle (process.ts:104-110; cli server-process.ts passes lifecycle in service mode only; 'unregistered servers sharing the database never sweep'). The timestamp guard restores equivalent pre-boot-only semantics for every boot mode without mode-gating serve.rs (out of lane scope). Residual (v2-shaped, not this regression): pending background records carry no timestamps, so cross-process replay interference is closed by v2's mode protocol, not by the guard — the sweep's recover_pending still skips locally-running jobs (in-process safe); orchestrator may consider lifecycle-gating the sweep to service mode as a follow-up for exact v2 parity. L01 unaffected: boot_sweep_recovers_orphans_at_boot (claim seeded before boot) and runtime_recovery 5/5 stay green; sweep still recovers genuine pre-boot orphans.
